result.title: Serialization Tax in Shared-Latent Exchangeable Decisions
result.summary: Accurate item probabilities can produce inaccurate group-level decisions. A system may score each item separately, yet act on whether enough hidden items succeed: show a slate, defer a panel decision, or inspect a batch. When items share an uncertain latent state, independent marginalization preserves means but removes dependence from the aggregate posterior. We call this error the serialization tax. For binary items sharing one success rate, classical convex-order comparisons give a more dispersed exact count law than any independent completion with the same total mean. We quantify variance and total-variation gaps, derive threshold separation under margin conditions, and connect posterior approximation to decision regret. Separate results cover non-binary outcomes, heterogeneous items, and sufficient posterior resolution. TaxScore identifies large hidden blocks with unresolved uncertainty near a decision boundary for routing to richer posterior heads. On pre-specified, hidden-target-free MovieLens 1M/10M audits, existing shared-latent heads improve high-score negative log-likelihood (NLL)/utility from 0.673/0.696 to 0.629/0.723 and from 0.670/0.691 to 0.639/0.715. Routing gives 0.006--0.012 full-population utility gains, with matched controls identifying their sources. Our code is available at https://github.com/SiminChang/Serialization-Tax-in-Shared-Latent-Exchangeable-Decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究共享潜在状态下的「序列化税」：逐项独立边缘化虽保留均值却抹去项间依赖，使组级决策失准；作者用凸序比较给出方差与全变差差距及阈值分离分析，并提出 TaxScore 把决策边界附近后验未解析的隐藏块路由到更强后验头，在 MovieLens 审计中验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「后验分辨率充分性」与「按边界不确定性路由到更丰富后验头」可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态精度、动态计算分配与停止决策的借鉴线索，但论文面向推荐系统组级决策，并非视觉推理本身。
